questions.question: In a man in his late 70s with two prior transcatheter aortic valves who developed recurrent dyspnea and fatigue, what echocardiographic and CT findings would establish severe prosthetic valve dysfunction severe enough to justify reintervention?

Three months after TAV-in-TAV, the patient presented with persistent fever, worsening heart failure symptoms, and a new increase in transprosthetic gradient. What differential diagnosis should be considered for early failure of a transcatheter bioprosthesis, and what findings in this case made Enterococcus faecalis prosthetic valve endocarditis the leading diagnosis?

Before offering a third transcatheter aortic valve procedure to a patient with prior prosthetic valve endocarditis, what clinical, microbiologic, and imaging evidence should be present to support that the infection has been adequately treated and is no longer active?
Which preprocedural CT measurements are most important when planning a TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV procedure, and how do they help predict coronary obstruction, neo-skirt risk, and future coronary access?

In this patient with treated prosthetic valve endocarditis, COPD, diabetes, recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding, prior PCI, a pacemaker, and two deeply integrated transcatheter valves, what factors made surgical explantation and redo root surgery less favorable than a third transcatheter intervention?
What was the procedural rationale for choosing a self-expanding Acurate neo2 valve and implanting it high, aligned with the prior Evolut leaflets, during the third valve procedure?
By what mechanisms can healed prosthetic valve endocarditis lead later to mixed prosthetic stenosis and regurgitation even after blood cultures have cleared and imaging shows no active infection?

Immediately after the third valve implantation, transthoracic echocardiography showed no regurgitation but a mean gradient of 67 mm Hg, an aortic valve area of 0.9 cm2, and a Doppler velocity index of 0.24; one month later the mean gradient had fallen to 27 mm Hg. How would you interpret this early physiology, and what mechanisms could explain the subsequent improvement?
